issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnRide() that returns a String (the problem text and the template call System.out.println(r.messageOnRide())). However, the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes (Pig, Seal) implement messageOnRide with an int parameter. This parameter mismatch would confuse students about which method to implement and causes the template Main example to be incompatible with the solution's API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the speed parameter: define Rideable.messageOnRide():String and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to specify and use messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the verbal specification of the return value accordingly. Prefer option A to preserve the current problem description and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a Rideable.messageOnRide() method with no parameters returning a String (used to produce "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). The solution repository instead defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it in Pig and Seal (returning strings that include "at [speed] mph"). This changes the conceptual contract of the Rideable behavior (adds a speed parameter and alters the expected return text), creating a mismatch students must resolve between the exercise description and the provided reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement: change Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to Rideable.messageOnRide() returning String, and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() that returns "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]". Alternatively, if an explicit speed parameter is intended, update the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the described expected output accordingly.
